newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds guided higher in '97 run up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds guided higher in '97 run up.

text.p: *Australian bond futures closed firm, helped on by further gains in U.S. Treasuries in Tokyo in the early part of the day.
*The local market is operating a half day on Tuesday.
*Treasury offering A$800 million of T-notes on Tuesday.
Australian bond futures closed firm, helped on by further gains in U.S. Treasuries during a shortened Tokyo session ahead of the Japanese New Year holiday, which spans the rest of the week.

However, local turnover remained seasonally subdued, and the absence of Japanese inquiry, which has been noticed in recent sessions, is likely to make Tuesday's pre-New Year half-day of trade a non-event, traders said.
"There's not a lot left to drive the market now until the New Year. I suspect we won't get back into full swing until next week," one trader added.

A sharp rally in U.S. Treasuries on Friday following a weaker than expected U.S. durable goods orders report and a surge in the U.S. dollar against the yen had sparked a bout of short-covering in U.S. debt in Tokyo.
The U.S. faces November leading indicators and existing homes sales later today.

Meanwhile, the Australian Treasury is offering a total of A$800 million of notes on Tuesday, comprising of A$200 million of five-week, A$200 million of 13-week and A$400 million of 26-week maturities.
The result will be announced at 2.00 p.m. (0300 GMT).

A late local squeeze saw yield spreads to the U.S. and New Zealand reverse an initial underperformce, although the Australia/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread now finding difficulty getting back below 110 basis points. Meanwhile, Canadian bond yields outpaced the bloc.

Bond futures, which had been trading the SYCOM system, remained entrenched in recent ranges, but the March bills contract broke resistance at 94.12 and 94.14, and now has the December 11 rate cut high of 94.19 in view.
